entities.name: PMID:25447994
observations: Yang et al. reported that an MKS transition-zone module (Cep290, Mks1, B9d1, and B9d2) migrates away from the centriole in Drosophila spermatids and remains associated with the growing axoneme tip.

The study concluded that this migrating ciliary gate compartmentalizes the site of axoneme assembly; Cep290 is required for transition-zone composition, axoneme-tip compartmentalization, and axoneme integrity.

entities.name: Migrating MKS gate
observations: In Drosophila spermatids, the MKS transition-zone domain moves distally away from the centriole as the axoneme elongates and remains associated with the growing axoneme tip.

This supports functional compartmentalization of the distal axoneme-assembly site rather than a merely stationary basal-body boundary; the evidence does not establish an absolutely impermeable barrier.
